title: Align graph animations to shared clock
summary: Aligned graph surface morph transitions to the shared animation kernel by adding graph motion-plan refs, a graph surface sampler, deterministic progress normalization, and WebGL consumption of the sampler.

sourceRefs.summary: Current graph transition interpolation code and likely first shared-clock adapter target.
2D scene and layout model used by graph renderers.
Semantic graph object model that should generate renderer-neutral graph frames.
Graph transition tests for interpolation semantics.
Adds graph surface motion-plan creation, shared-clock sampler, sampled-frame metadata, and kernel progress normalization.
Routes WebGL surface morph scene models through the graph sampler instead of direct interpolation.
Covers renderer-neutral graph motion plans, deterministic rewind sampling, and progress clamping.

verification: npm test -- tests/graph-transitions.test.ts tests/graph-webgl.test.ts tests/graph-2d-scene.test.ts tests/rendering.test.ts
expectedLearning: How much of the equation sampled-frame clock can be reused directly by graph, vector, surface, and projection animations.
Where SVG and WebGL graph renderers need separate view adapters while sharing semantic time and layout state.
allowedWork: Create a graph animation adapter that samples semantic graph transitions through the shared clock/progress protocol.
Keep SVG and WebGL renderers consuming explicit frames rather than owning semantic timing.
Add tests that prove graph frames are deterministic and rewindable.
disallowedWork: Do not replace Three.js/WebGL renderer internals unless the shared clock boundary requires a small adapter.
Do not build new graph authoring UI before the protocol is visible in tests.
Do not implement a full graph layout engine in this slice.
